name: Tiger Woods
hints: Turned pro in 1996 and was PGA Tour Player of the Year a record number of times.
Born in Cypress, California, and played college golf at Stanford before turning pro.
Has won 15 major championships, second all-time only to Jack Nicklaus.
Long associated with Nike and famous for wearing a red shirt on Sunday.
Held all four major titles at once during 2000-2001, a feat nicknamed after him.
Completed one of sports' greatest comebacks by winning the 2019 Masters after years of injury.

name: Jack Nicklaus
hints: Turned pro in 1961 after a standout amateur career at Ohio State.
Born in Columbus, Ohio, and known for his powerful, high ball flight.
Holds the record for most men's major championships won, with 18.
Also one of the most prolific golf course designers in history.
Nicknamed 'The Golden Bear' for his blond hair and build.
His epic 1986 Masters win at age 46 is considered one of golf's greatest moments.

name: Arnold Palmer
hints: Turned pro in 1954 and helped popularize golf on television.
Born in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, the son of a golf course superintendent.
Won 7 major championships and 62 PGA Tour events overall.
His army of passionate fans became famously known as 'Arnie's Army.'
Nicknamed 'The King,' he also lent his name to a half-lemonade, half-iced-tea drink.
One of the 'Big Three' golfers of the 1960s alongside Nicklaus and Player.

name: Gary Player
hints: Turned pro in 1953 and became known for his relentless fitness regimen.
Born in Johannesburg, South Africa, one of the sport's first true global stars.
Won 9 major championships across three different decades.
Almost always wore all black on the course.
Nicknamed 'The Black Knight' or 'Mr. Fitness.'
One of only five golfers to complete the career Grand Slam, alongside Nicklaus, Hogan, Sarazen, and Woods.

name: Tom Watson
hints: Turned pro in 1971 after graduating from Stanford.
Born in Kansas City, Missouri, and known for his excellent links golf.
Won 8 major championships, including 5 Open Championships.
Engaged in a legendary head-to-head battle with Jack Nicklaus at the 1977 Open, the 'Duel in the Sun.'
Nearly won an improbable 6th Open Championship in 2009 at age 59.
Famous for chipping in on the 17th hole to win the 1982 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach.

name: Seve Ballesteros
hints: Turned pro in 1974 as a teenager from a farming family.
Born in Pedrena, Spain, and famed for his flair and creative recovery shots.
Won 5 major championships, including the Masters twice.
A driving force behind Europe's Ryder Cup resurgence, both as player and captain.
Won the 1979 Open Championship partly from a parking lot, earning the nickname 'the car park champion.'
Widely considered the most charismatic European golfer of his generation.

name: Nick Faldo
hints: Turned pro in 1976 and later rebuilt his swing from scratch mid-career.
Born in Welwyn Garden City, England, known for meticulous, disciplined play.
Won 6 major championships, including 3 Masters titles.
Famously outlasted Greg Norman's final-round collapse to win the 1996 Masters.
Went on to become a leading golf broadcaster after his playing career.
Captained Europe's Ryder Cup team in 2008.

name: Greg Norman
hints: Turned pro in 1976 and spent 331 total weeks ranked world No. 1.
Born in Mount Isa, Queensland, Australia.
Won 2 major championships, both Open Championships.
Known for his aggressive play and bleach-blond hair.
Nicknamed 'The Shark,' with a logo to match.
Later became the driving force and CEO behind the LIV Golf league.

name: Phil Mickelson
hints: Turned pro in 1992 and won a PGA Tour event while still an amateur.
Born in San Diego, California, and plays left-handed despite being right-handed otherwise.
Won 6 major championships, including 3 Masters titles.
Became the oldest major champion in history at the 2021 PGA Championship, age 50.
Nicknamed 'Lefty,' known for his go-for-broke style and fan-friendly demeanor.
Left the PGA Tour to become a founding star of the LIV Golf league in 2022.

name: Ernie Els
hints: Turned pro in 1989 and is known for one of the smoothest swings in golf.
Born in Johannesburg, South Africa.
Won 4 major championships, including 2 U.S. Opens and 2 Open Championships.
Nicknamed 'The Big Easy' for his relaxed tempo and demeanor.
Also built a successful wine and golf course design business.
Won the 2012 Open Championship after Adam Scott bogeyed the last four holes.

name: Vijay Singh
hints: Turned pro in 1982 and became famous for hitting more range balls than anyone on tour.
Born in Lautoka, Fiji, the first male golfer from Asia to reach world No. 1.
Won 3 major championships, including 2 PGA Championships.
Named PGA Tour Player of the Year in 2004 at age 41.
Known simply as 'Vijay' to golf fans worldwide.
Won 9 PGA Tour events in his standout 2004 season.

name: Padraig Harrington
hints: Turned pro in 1995 after a career as an accountant.
Born in Dublin, Ireland, known for his relentless work ethic on the range.
Won 3 major championships in a two-year span, 2007-2008.
Won back-to-back Open Championships, the first European to do so in decades.
Later captained Europe's Ryder Cup team in 2021.
Has become a dominant force on the PGA Tour Champions in his 50s.

name: Justin Leonard
hints: Turned pro in 1994 after an outstanding amateur career at the University of Texas.
Born in Dallas, Texas.
Won 1 major championship, the 1997 Open Championship at Royal Troon.
Sank a legendary long birdie putt on the 17th hole at Brookline in the 1999 Ryder Cup.
That putt sparked a wild celebration that overran the green before Jose Maria Olazabal could putt.
Known for one of the greatest comeback wins in Ryder Cup history, the 'Miracle at Brookline.'

name: Davis Love III
hints: Turned pro in 1985, the son of a PGA teaching professional.
Born in Charlotte, North Carolina, known for his smooth, powerful swing.
Won 1 major championship, the 1997 PGA Championship.
Captained the U.S. Ryder Cup team in both 2012 and 2016.
Won 21 PGA Tour titles over a two-decade career.
One of the most respected veterans and Ryder Cup figures of his generation.

name: Fred Couples
hints: Turned pro in 1980 and became known for one of the most effortless swings in golf.
Born in Seattle, Washington.
Won 1 major championship, the 1992 Masters.
Nicknamed 'Boom Boom' for his prodigious driving distance.
Was world No. 1 and PGA Player of the Year in 1991-92.
Remains a fan favorite and dominant force on the PGA Tour Champions.

name: Payne Stewart
hints: Turned pro in 1979 and was instantly recognizable for his old-fashioned style.
Born in Springfield, Missouri.
Won 3 major championships, including 2 U.S. Opens.
Famous for wearing plus-fours (knickers) and colorful tam o'shanter caps on course.
Won the 1999 U.S. Open at Pinehurst with a dramatic final-hole putt.
Died tragically in a plane crash just months after that final major win.

name: Ben Hogan
hints: Turned pro in the 1930s and became renowned for his precise ball-striking.
Born in Dublin, Texas, and rose from a difficult childhood to golf greatness.
Won 9 major championships despite a near-fatal car accident in 1949.
Won 3 majors in a single year, 1953, later dubbed the 'Triple Crown.'
His life story was depicted in the film 'Follow the Sun.'
Regarded as one of the greatest ball-strikers ever, author of 'Five Lessons: The Modern Fundamentals of Golf.'

name: Sam Snead
hints: Turned pro in 1934 and played competitively into his 60s.
Born in Ashwood, Virginia, known for one of the most naturally fluid swings ever.
Won 7 major championships and holds the record for most PGA Tour wins, 82.
Nicknamed 'Slammin' Sammy' for his power off the tee.
Famous for his trademark straw hat.
Never won the U.S. Open despite finishing runner-up four times.

name: Byron Nelson
hints: Turned pro in 1932 and later became a respected golf broadcaster.
Born in Fort Worth, Texas.
Won 5 major championships in a relatively short competitive career.
Won an astonishing 11 consecutive PGA Tour events in 1945, a record that still stands.
Won 18 total events that same year, also a still-standing record.
A PGA Tour event, the AT&T Byron Nelson, is named in his honor.

name: Bobby Jones
hints: Never turned professional, remaining an amateur his entire competitive career.
Born in Atlanta, Georgia, and trained originally as a lawyer.
Won 7 major championships (by modern count) purely as an amateur golfer.
Completed the original Grand Slam in 1930, winning all four majors of that era in one year.
Retired from competition at just 28, right after that Grand Slam.
Co-founded Augusta National Golf Club and the Masters Tournament.

name: Walter Hagen
hints: Turned pro in 1912 and helped elevate professional golfers' social standing.
Born in Rochester, New York.
Won 11 major championships, including 5 PGA Championships.
Nicknamed 'The Haig,' famous for his flamboyant lifestyle and showmanship.
Won 4 consecutive PGA Championships from 1924-1927.
Often credited with popularizing golf as a viable, glamorous profession.

name: Rory McIlroy
hints: Turned pro in 2007 as a teenager out of Holywood, Northern Ireland.
Known for his combination of power off the tee and smooth tempo.
Won his first major, the 2011 U.S. Open, by a record-setting margin.
Spent years chasing the career Grand Slam after winning three of the four majors by his mid-20s.
Finally completed the career Grand Slam by winning the 2025 Masters in a playoff.
Widely regarded as the leading European golfer of his generation.

name: Jon Rahm
hints: Turned pro in 2016 after a standout college career at Arizona State.
Born in Barrika, Spain, and known for his fiery intensity on course.
Won the 2021 U.S. Open and the 2023 Masters.
Was born with a clubfoot, giving him an unusually short, powerful swing.
Left the PGA Tour for a lucrative move to LIV Golf in late 2023.
Often mentioned alongside Seve Ballesteros as Spain's greatest golfing talent.

name: Scottie Scheffler
hints: Turned pro in 2018 after an All-American career at the University of Texas.
Born in Ridgewood, New Jersey, but raised in Dallas, Texas.
Known for spending long stretches as the world's top-ranked golfer.
Has won multiple Masters titles, including in 2022 and 2024.
Known for an unorthodox, rock-solid putting grip and a quiet, methodical demeanor.
Widely regarded as the most dominant golfer in the world in the mid-2020s.

name: Jordan Spieth
hints: Turned pro in 2012 after starring at the University of Texas.
Born in Dallas, Texas, known for his exceptional putting and course management.
Won 3 of the 4 majors before turning 24, missing only the PGA Championship.
Suffered a painful final-round collapse at the 2016 Masters after leading by 5 shots.
Won the 2015 Masters and 2015 U.S. Open in the same season.
Has spent years chasing the career Grand Slam, needing only the PGA Championship.

name: Justin Thomas
hints: Turned pro in 2013, the son of a PGA club professional.
Born in Louisville, Kentucky, and close childhood friends with Jordan Spieth.
Has won 2 PGA Championships, in 2017 and 2022.
Shot a record-tying 59 in a PGA Tour round early in his career.
Known simply by his initials, 'JT,' among fans and fellow players.
A key member of recent U.S. Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup teams.

name: Dustin Johnson
hints: Turned pro in 2007 and became known for elite athleticism and effortless power.
Born in Columbia, South Carolina.
Won the 2016 U.S. Open and the 2020 Masters.
Spent over 130 weeks ranked world No. 1 across his career.
Won the pandemic-delayed 2020 Masters by a record 5 strokes in November.
Left the PGA Tour to become a founding LIV Golf star in 2022.

name: Brooks Koepka
hints: Turned pro in 2012 and built his early career playing on European and Challenge Tours.
Born in West Palm Beach, Florida, known for elite fitness and a calm demeanor under pressure.
Has won 5 major championships, including back-to-back U.S. Opens in 2017-2018.
Also won back-to-back PGA Championships in 2018-2019.
Known for saving his best golf specifically for major championship weeks.
Won the 2023 PGA Championship as one of LIV Golf's biggest stars.

name: Collin Morikawa
hints: Turned pro in 2019 after an outstanding college career at Cal Berkeley.
Born in Los Angeles, California, known for extremely precise iron play.
Won the 2020 PGA Championship in just his second career major start.
Also won the 2021 Open Championship at Royal St George's.
Considered one of the most accurate ball-strikers of his generation.
Won two different major championships before turning 25.

name: Xander Schauffele
hints: Turned pro in 2015 after playing college golf at San Diego State.
Born in San Diego, California, to a French father and Japanese-American mother.
Won Olympic gold in golf at the 2021 Tokyo Games.
Spent years as one of the best players without a major before breaking through.
Won both the PGA Championship and the Open Championship in 2024.
Known for a relaxed, understated personality despite his elite results.

name: Bryson DeChambeau
hints: Turned pro in 2016 after winning the NCAA title and U.S. Amateur in the same year.
Born in Modesto, California, nicknamed 'The Scientist' for his analytical approach.
Famously bulked up dramatically to add driving distance in 2020.
Won the 2020 U.S. Open at Winged Foot after that transformation.
Left the PGA Tour to join LIV Golf in 2022.
Won a second U.S. Open in 2024 at Pinehurst with a dramatic closing bunker shot.

name: Viktor Hovland
hints: Turned pro in 2019 after winning the U.S. Amateur while at Oklahoma State.
Born in Oslo, Norway, one of the country's first true golf stars.
Known for elite ball-striking paired with a famously inconsistent short game for years.
Was low amateur at the 2019 Masters before turning professional.
A fan favorite for his outgoing, chatty personality on course.
Has emerged as one of the world's top-ranked players without yet winning a major.

name: Matt Fitzpatrick
hints: Turned pro in 2014 after winning the U.S. Amateur while at Northwestern.
Born in Sheffield, England.
Won the 2013 U.S. Amateur at Brookline.
Returned to that same course nine years later and won the 2022 U.S. Open there.
Known for one of the most compact, repeatable swings on tour.
Became the first golfer to win both the U.S. Amateur and U.S. Open at the same course.

name: Shane Lowry
hints: Turned pro in 2009 after winning the Irish Open as an amateur.
Born in Clara, County Offaly, Ireland.
Won the 2019 Open Championship at Royal Portrush, Northern Ireland's first Open in decades.
Won that title in front of an emotional, deafening home crowd.
Known for his warm, easygoing personality off the course.
A key contributor to recent European Ryder Cup teams.

name: Francesco Molinari
hints: Turned pro in 2002 and played alongside his brother Edoardo for years.
Born in Turin, Italy.
Won the 2018 Open Championship at Carnoustie.
Became the first Italian golfer ever to win a major championship.
Went undefeated in five matches at the 2018 Ryder Cup.
Famous for his metronomic, error-free ball-striking during his 2018 peak.

name: Adam Scott
hints: Turned pro in 2000 after being mentored early on by Greg Norman.
Born in Adelaide, Australia.
Won the 2013 Masters in a playoff after a dramatic birdie putt.
Became the first Australian ever to win the Masters.
Was among the first prominent players to popularize the long, anchored putter.
Reached world No. 1 in 2014 after years as one of the game's smoothest swingers.

name: Sergio Garcia
hints: Turned pro in 1999 as a teenage prodigy from Spain.
Born in Borriol, Spain, nicknamed 'El Nino' for his youthful breakthrough.
Spent nearly two decades as one of the best players without a major title.
Finally broke through by winning the 2017 Masters in a playoff.
Emotional win came on what would have been Seve Ballesteros's 60th birthday.
Later joined LIV Golf as a team captain and owner.

name: Henrik Stenson
hints: Turned pro in 1999 and became known for one of the purest iron games in golf.
Born in Gothenburg, Sweden.
Won a legendary duel with Phil Mickelson at the 2016 Open Championship.
Both players shattered the previous major championship scoring record that week.
Became the first Swedish golfer to win a men's major championship.
Later served as the inaugural European captain courted by LIV Golf.

name: Zach Johnson
hints: Turned pro in 1998 after college golf at Drake University.
Born in Iowa City, Iowa, known for his precise short game despite modest length.
Won the 2007 Masters by consistently laying up on the par-5s all week.
Also won the 2015 Open Championship at St Andrews in a playoff.
Known for his devout faith, often referencing it in victory speeches.
Later served as U.S. Ryder Cup captain in 2023.

name: Keegan Bradley
hints: Turned pro in 2008 after college golf at St. John's University.
Born in Woodstock, Vermont, nephew of LPGA Hall of Famer Pat Bradley.
Won the 2011 PGA Championship in his first career major start.
Was one of the last prominent players to use a long, anchored putter before it was banned.
Named U.S. Ryder Cup captain for the 2025 matches.
Pushed to make himself a playing captain, an idea much discussed in golf media.

name: John Daly
hints: A fan-favorite nicknamed the PGAs 'Wild Thing'.
He won his local club championship at 13 years old.
Holds the record for the highest score on a single hole at a PGA tour event (18).
Known as the heaviest drinker on the tour, he was often drunk during tournaments.
He won the 1991 PGA Championship as a ninth alternate after driving through the night to make it.
His unorthodox swing made him one of the longest hitters on the tour, with the club being almost vertical at the apex.

name: Gene Sarazen
hints: Turned pro in 1920 and is credited with inventing the modern sand wedge.
Born in Harrison, New York, to Italian immigrant parents.
Won 7 major championships across the 1920s and 1930s.
One of only five golfers to complete the career Grand Slam.
Nicknamed 'The Squire' for his dapper on-course style.
Famous for holing a 4-wood for double eagle on the 15th at the 1935 Masters, the 'shot heard round the world.'

name: Lee Trevino
hints: Turned pro in 1960 after growing up caddying near Dallas, Texas.
Born in Dallas, Texas, to a family of modest means.
Won 6 major championships, including 2 U.S. Opens and 2 Open Championships.
Known for his quick wit and constant chatter with fans and playing partners.
Nicknamed 'The Merry Mex' or 'Super Mex.'
Survived being struck by lightning at the 1975 Western Open.

name: Raymond Floyd
hints: Turned pro in 1961 and had one of the longest winning careers in golf history.
Born in Fort Bragg, North Carolina.
Won 4 major championships spanning from 1969 to 1986.
Won the 1976 Masters by 8 shots, tying the tournament's 72-hole record at the time.
Became the oldest U.S. Open champion in history when he won in 1986 at age 43.
A fierce competitor known for his intense on-course stare.

name: Hale Irwin
hints: Turned pro in 1968 after also playing college football as a defensive back.
Born in Joplin, Missouri.
Won 3 U.S. Open championships across three different decades.
Famous for a joyous, high-fiving sprint down the 18th fairway after a clinching putt in 1990.
Became the oldest U.S. Open champion ever at the time, winning in 1990 at age 45.
One of the most dominant players in PGA Tour Champions history after turning 50.

name: Curtis Strange
hints: Turned pro in 1976 after a standout college career at Wake Forest.
Born in Norfolk, Virginia.
Won back-to-back U.S. Opens in 1988 and 1989.
Was the first golfer to do that since Ben Hogan in the early 1950s.
Later became a respected golf broadcaster.
Captained the U.S. Ryder Cup team in 2002.

name: Mark O'Meara
hints: Turned pro in 1980 and became one of Isleworth's most recognizable club members.
Born in Goldsboro, North Carolina, and close friends with a young Tiger Woods.
Won both the Masters and the Open Championship in the same year, 1998.
Did so at age 41, making him one of the oldest first-time major champions.
Won the Open at Royal Birkdale in a four-hole playoff.
Widely credited as an early mentor to Tiger Woods.

name: Ian Woosnam
hints: Turned pro in 1976 despite being one of the shortest players on tour.
Born in Oswestry, Wales, known for prodigious power from a compact frame.
Won 1 major championship, the 1991 Masters.
Nicknamed 'Woosie' by fans and fellow players.
Reached world No. 1 the same year he won the Masters.
Later captained Europe's victorious 2006 Ryder Cup team.

name: Sandy Lyle
hints: Turned pro in 1977 after a standout amateur career in Scotland and England.
Born in Shrewsbury, England, to a Scottish golf professional father.
Won 2 major championships, the 1985 Open and 1988 Masters.
Became the first British golfer ever to win the Masters.
Famously hit a 7-iron from a fairway bunker to set up his winning birdie at Augusta.
A key figure in Europe's Ryder Cup resurgence of the 1980s.

name: Bernhard Langer
hints: Turned pro in 1972 and battled the putting yips multiple times across his career.
Born in Anhausen, West Germany.
Won 2 Masters titles, in 1985 and 1993.
Became the first German golfer to win a major championship.
Widely regarded as the greatest player in PGA Tour Champions history.
Continued winning senior majors well into his 60s.

name: Jose Maria Olazabal
hints: Turned pro in 1985 and formed a legendary Ryder Cup partnership with Seve Ballesteros.
Born in Hondarribia, Spain.
Won 2 Masters titles, in 1994 and 1999.
Overcame a severe case of rheumatoid arthritis in his feet mid-career to keep competing.
Later captained Europe's emotional 2012 Ryder Cup win, dedicated to Seve.
Considered one of the greatest short-game players of his generation.

name: Corey Pavin
hints: Turned pro in 1982 after a decorated amateur career at UCLA.
Born in Oxnard, California, known for elite shot-making despite modest length.
Won 1 major championship, the 1995 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills.
Famously hit a 4-wood to four feet on the final hole to seal that win.
Captained the U.S. Ryder Cup team in 2010.
Known throughout his career for a scrappy, creative short game.

name: Retief Goosen
hints: Turned pro in 1990 and survived being struck by lightning as a teenager.
Born in Pietersburg, South Africa.
Won 2 U.S. Open championships, in 2001 and 2004.
Nicknamed 'The Goose,' known for an unflappable, ice-cool demeanor.
Won his first U.S. Open after a dramatic 18-hole playoff.
One of the calmest putters under pressure of his generation.

name: Angel Cabrera
hints: Turned pro in 1989 after working as a caddie in his native Argentina.
Born in Cordoba, Argentina.
Won both the 2007 U.S. Open and the 2009 Masters.
Became the first golfer from Argentina to win a major championship.
Nicknamed 'El Pato' ('The Duck').
Beat Kenny Perry and Chad Campbell in a playoff to win the 2009 Masters.

name: Y.E. Yang
hints: Turned pro in 1996 after starting golf relatively late as a teenager.
Born in Jeju, South Korea.
Won 1 major championship, the 2009 PGA Championship.
Became the first golfer born in Asia to win a men's major title.
Achieved that win by defeating Tiger Woods in the final round, the only time Tiger lost a major with a 54-hole lead.
Hit a memorable hybrid approach on the final hole to seal the upset.

name: Charl Schwartzel
hints: Turned pro in 2002 after a standout junior career in South Africa.
Born in Johannesburg, South Africa.
Won 1 major championship, the 2011 Masters.
Closed with four consecutive birdies on the back nine to win that Masters.
Later became a prominent figure and event winner on LIV Golf.
Part of a strong generation of South African major champions.

name: Bubba Watson
hints: Turned pro in 2003 and is entirely self-taught, having never taken a formal golf lesson.
Born in Bagdad, Florida, known for enormous, curving shot shapes.
Won 2 Masters titles, in 2012 and 2014.
Plays left-handed despite doing most other things right-handed.
Famously won the 2012 Masters with a miracle hooking wedge shot from the trees in a playoff.
Also known for his pink driver and quirky personality.

name: Danny Willett
hints: Turned pro in 2008 after a strong amateur career in England.
Born in Sheffield, England.
Won 1 major championship, the 2016 Masters.
Nearly missed the tournament entirely, only playing because of the birth of his first son.
Capitalized on a historic final-round collapse by the 54-hole leader to win.
Became the first English golfer to win the Masters since Nick Faldo.

name: Patrick Reed
hints: Turned pro in 2011 after a standout, if controversial, college career.
Born in San Antonio, Texas.
Won 1 major championship, the 2018 Masters.
Nicknamed 'Captain America' for his fiery Ryder Cup performances.
Held off Rickie Fowler down the stretch to win that Masters green jacket.
Later became one of the first prominent players to join LIV Golf.

name: Gary Woodland
hints: Turned pro in 2007 after playing college basketball before switching fully to golf.
Born in Topeka, Kansas, known for elite athleticism and long drives.
Won 1 major championship, the 2019 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach.
Held off a hard-charging Brooks Koepka down the stretch to win.
Later underwent brain surgery in 2023 for a condition affecting his daily life.
Returned to competitive golf as an emotional comeback story after that surgery.

name: Jason Day
hints: Turned pro in 2006 after emigrating from Australia to the U.S. as a teenager to train.
Born in Beaudesert, Australia.
Won 1 major championship, the 2015 PGA Championship, with a record low score.
Reached world No. 1 shortly after that breakthrough win.
Known for a distinctive pre-shot routine involving closed eyes and visualization.
One of the most talented ball-strikers of his golden mid-2010s stretch.

name: Louis Oosthuizen
hints: Turned pro in 2002 and grew up near the same course as fellow South African stars.
Born in Mossel Bay, South Africa.
Won 1 major championship, the 2010 Open Championship at St Andrews, by 7 shots.
Has finished runner-up at all four majors at various points in his career.
Famous for an ace on the par-5 second hole at Augusta via a hosel-hit shot in 2012.
Later became a prominent LIV Golf player and team captain.

name: Wyndham Clark
hints: Turned pro in 2017 after college golf at Oregon and Oklahoma State.
Born in Denver, Colorado.
Won 1 major championship, the 2023 U.S. Open at Los Angeles Country Club.
Held off Rory McIlroy down the stretch in the final round to win.
Broke through relatively late for a major winner, in his late 20s.
Has spoken openly about the loss of his mother as a driving motivation.

name: Brian Harman
hints: Turned pro in 2009 after a standout college career at Georgia.
Born in Savannah, Georgia, one of the shorter hitters on tour.
Won 1 major championship, the 2023 Open Championship at Royal Liverpool.
Won wire-to-wire, leading after every round of the tournament.
Plays left-handed and is known for elite bunker and scrambling skills.
Won that Open by six shots, a surprisingly dominant margin.

name: Jason Dufner
hints: Turned pro in 2000 after college golf at Auburn.
Born in Cleveland, Ohio, known for an unusually flat, deadpan expression on course.
Won 1 major championship, the 2013 PGA Championship.
His slumped, disinterested-looking sitting pose briefly became an internet meme called 'Dufnering.'
Considered one of the more understated, low-key major champions of his era.
Known for a smooth, compact swing built for consistency.

name: Michael Campbell
hints: Turned pro in 1993 and represented New Zealand throughout his career.
Born in Hastings, New Zealand, of Maori descent.
Won 1 major championship, the 2005 U.S. Open at Pinehurst.
Beat Tiger Woods by two shots to win that title.
Became just the second golfer from New Zealand to win a men's major.
His win remains one of the more surprising major upsets of the 2000s.

name: Ben Curtis
hints: Turned pro in 2000 and was playing in his very first major championship start.
Born in Ostrander, Ohio.
Won 1 major championship, the 2003 Open Championship at Royal St George's.
Was ranked 396th in the world at the time, one of the biggest upsets in major history.
Remains the only golfer to win a major on his first career start.
His win stunned a leaderboard full of far more established stars.

name: Trevor Immelman
hints: Turned pro in 1999 after a strong junior and amateur career in South Africa.
Born in Cape Town, South Africa.
Won 1 major championship, the 2008 Masters.
Held off a hard-charging Tiger Woods in the final round to win his green jacket.
Later transitioned into a prominent role as a golf broadcaster.
Now a lead commentator for CBS's golf coverage.

name: Stewart Cink
hints: Turned pro in 1995 after college golf at Georgia Tech.
Born in Huntsville, Alabama.
Won 1 major championship, the 2009 Open Championship at Turnberry.
Beat 59-year-old Tom Watson in a playoff after Watson nearly won at almost 60.
Later became a two-time winner well into his 40s during the pandemic era.
Known for his tall frame and easygoing demeanor.

name: Graeme McDowell
hints: Turned pro in 2002 after a standout amateur career in Northern Ireland.
Born in Portrush, Northern Ireland.
Won 1 major championship, the 2010 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach.
Became the first European golfer to win the U.S. Open in 40 years.
Nicknamed 'G-Mac' by fans and broadcasters.
A key clutch performer for Europe across several Ryder Cups.

name: Darren Clarke
hints: Turned pro in 1990 and became one of Northern Ireland's most beloved golfers.
Born in Dungannon, Northern Ireland.
Won 1 major championship, the 2011 Open Championship at Royal St George's.
Won it at age 42, considered a career-crowning achievement after years of near-misses.
A close friend and mentor figure to fellow Northern Irish stars Rory McIlroy and Graeme McDowell.
Later captained Europe's Ryder Cup team in 2016.

name: Cameron Smith
hints: Turned pro in 2013 after a standout junior career in Australia.
Born in Brisbane, Australia, known for one of the best putting strokes in golf.
Won 1 major championship, the 2022 Open Championship at St Andrews.
Shot a final-round 64 at the Old Course to overtake Cameron Young and Rory McIlroy.
Instantly recognizable for his signature mullet hairstyle.
Left the PGA Tour to join LIV Golf shortly after that major win.
